source.stem:
Plant cells are often green but animal cells are not usually green.
Which structure in plant cells makes them green?

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: producer is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: An organism that performs photosynthesis is classified as a producer.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when An organism that performs photosynthesis is classified as a producer is not true.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Judge from the most visible feature in the figure, not from the mechanism's test.

intelligence.enrichment: Plants make their own food by photosynthesis and are producers or autotrophs; organisms that cannot make their own food are consumers. An organism's food source determines its feeding role in the ecosystem. The learner correctly applies this rule: Plants make their own food by photosynthesis and are producers or autotrophs; organisms that cannot make their own food are consumers. Consumer means any organism that uses food, so plants and animals are consumers in the same way.
